w5-tf-0.en: Every new business is a start-up.
w5-tf-0.q: 每家新企业都是初创企业（start-up）。

w5-tf-1.en: A biotech spin-out with a patent but no product yet can still be classified as a start-up.
w5-tf-1.q: 一家拥有专利但尚无产品的生物技术衍生公司（spin-out），仍然可以被归类为初创企业（start-up）。

w5-tf-2.en: The lecture argues that entrepreneurial requirements such as action and persistence are fixed personality traits one is born with.
w5-tf-2.q: 课程认为，行动力和坚持等创业要求是与生俱来、固定不变的人格特质。

w5-tf-3.en: According to the lecture, industry experience often predicts entrepreneurial success better than youth.
w5-tf-3.q: 根据课程内容，行业经验往往比年轻更能预测创业成功。

w5-tf-4.en: The lecture claims a brilliant idea is the main factor separating successful from unsuccessful ventures.
w5-tf-4.q: 课程声称，一个绝妙的想法是区分成功与失败企业的主要因素。

w5-tf-5.en: Small firms beat incumbents mainly because of speed, focus and flexibility rather than greater resources, and this advantage is permanent.
w5-tf-5.q: 小公司击败在位企业（incumbents）主要靠速度、专注和灵活性，而不是更多的资源，而且这种优势是永久的。

w5-tf-6.en: In the lecture's view, if you cannot name the first customer, you have a theme rather than an opportunity.
w5-tf-6.q: 课程认为，如果你说不出第一个客户是谁，那你拥有的只是一个主题，而不是一个机会。

w5-tf-7.en: Because AI lowers the cost of building products, production becomes less scarce while distribution, trust and judgment become key bottlenecks.
w5-tf-7.q: 由于 AI 降低了构建产品的成本，生产变得不那么稀缺，而分销、信任和判断力成为关键瓶颈。

w5-tf-8.en: The lecture reports that 18.5% of US adults starting a business and 5.5% established ownership can be read as a precise cohort survival rate.
w5-tf-8.q: 课程报告称，18.5% 的美国成年人正在创业、5.5% 拥有成熟企业，这两个数字可以被解读为一个精确的同期群（cohort）存活率。

w5-tf-9.en: A verbal expression of interest from a potential customer is stronger evidence of demand than a paid deposit or signed letter of intent.
w5-tf-9.q: 潜在客户口头表示感兴趣，比支付定金或签署意向书（letter of intent）更能证明存在需求。

w5-tf-10.en: Debt is cheaper if the venture succeeds and dangerous if it does not; equity is the reverse.
w5-tf-10.q: 如果企业成功，债务（debt）更便宜；如果企业失败，债务就很危险；股权（equity）则正好相反。

w5-tf-11.en: Government grants such as the R&D Tax Incentive are strictly a form of debt financing.
w5-tf-11.q: 研发税收激励（R&D Tax Incentive）等政府补助严格来说属于债务融资（debt financing）。

w5-tf-12.en: The failure-reason percentages for closed venture-backed companies (70%, 43%, 29%, 19%) cannot be added together because one company can report several reasons.
w5-tf-12.q: 已关闭的风险投资支持公司的失败原因百分比（70%、43%、29%、19%）不能相加，因为一家公司可以报告多个原因。

w5-tf-13.en: Bringing in professional managers at the take-off stage signals that the founder has failed.
w5-tf-13.q: 在起飞期（take-off）引入职业经理人，标志着创始人失败了。

w5-tf-14.en: Crowdfunding can simultaneously provide capital and test whether customers are willing to make a real commitment.
w5-tf-14.q: 众筹（crowdfunding）可以在提供资金的同时，检验客户是否愿意做出真实的承诺。

w5-mcq-0.en: Which of the following is MOST likely to be classified as a start-up rather than a small business?
enOptions: A two-person HR consultancy charging by the day
w5-mcq-0.q: 以下哪一项最有可能被归类为初创企业（start-up），而不是小企业（small business）？
options: Braddon 的一家单店咖啡馆
一家按天收费的两人人力资源咨询公司
一款面向手艺人的预约应用
一家新开的本地面包店

w5-mcq-1.en: A founder asks: "If demand doubled overnight, could we serve twice the customers without doubling staff?" This question tests whether the business is:
w5-mcq-1.q: 一位创始人问：「如果需求一夜之间翻倍，我们能否在员工不翻倍的情况下服务两倍的客户？」这个问题检验的是企业是否：

w5-mcq-2.en: After being made redundant, Tom becomes a sole trader mainly so that he has some income. Using the growth-intent typology, Tom is a:
w5-mcq-2.q: Tom 被裁员后成为个体经营者，主要是为了有些收入。按照成长意图分类（growth-intent typology），Tom 属于：
options: 生活方式型创业者（lifestyle entrepreneur）

w5-mcq-3.en: In the survey of what owners find most rewarding, which group values work–life balance most?
w5-mcq-3.q: 在关于企业主认为什么最有回报的调查中，哪一类人最看重工作与生活的平衡？

w5-mcq-4.en: Canva began as Fusion Books, an online yearbook design tool for schools. What lesson does the lecture draw from this?
enOptions: Start with a general product for everyone
Start with a specific first customer, learn, then expand to a general scalable product
w5-mcq-4.q: Canva 起步时叫 Fusion Books，是一款面向学校的在线毕业纪念册设计工具。课程从中得出什么教训？
options: 从一个面向所有人的通用产品开始
不惜一切代价避开投资者
随意转型直到有东西奏效
从一个具体的第一个客户开始，边做边学，再扩展为通用、可规模化的产品

w5-mcq-5.en: Atlassian priced its software so developers could buy it without complex approval and launched using credit cards. What does the lecture say external capital later bought?
w5-mcq-5.q: Atlassian 给软件定价，使开发者无需复杂审批就能购买，并靠信用卡起家。课程说后来的外部资本买到的是什么？
options: 创始人对董事会的控制权

w5-mcq-6.en: A student notices rising interest in fitness tracking and says, "Health is a huge trend, so I have an opportunity." What is the key weakness in this reasoning?
enOptions: Trends are never useful for entrepreneurs
Health is not a growing market
A trend becomes an opportunity only with a specific need, a value-creating product and a named first customer
w5-mcq-6.q: 一名学生注意到人们对健身追踪的兴趣日益增长，就说：「健康是一个巨大的趋势，所以我有了一个机会。」这一推理的关键缺陷是什么？
options: 趋势对创业者从来没用
健康不是一个增长中的市场
趋势只有在具备具体需求、能创造价值的产品和一个具名的第一个客户时，才会成为机会
机会首先需要风险投资

w5-mcq-7.en: According to the lecture, what fundamentally changed entrepreneurial logic when comparing 2005 with 2026?
enOptions: The cost of being wrong has fallen
Distribution has become easier than building
Bank loans have become more accessible
Founders now need larger engineering teams
w5-mcq-7.q: 根据课程内容，比较 2005 年和 2026 年，从根本上改变创业逻辑的是什么？
options: 分销变得比构建更容易
银行贷款变得更容易获得
创始人现在需要更大的工程团队

w5-mcq-8.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the four advantages that remain scarce in the AI era?
w5-mcq-8.q: 以下哪一项不属于在 AI 时代仍然稀缺的四种优势之一？
options: 专有数据和关系（proprietary data and relationships）

w5-mcq-9.en: A six-person AI start-up lets each employee decide whether to paste customer records into public AI tools. Which AI-era management rule is most directly violated?
enOptions: Write data rules before the first customer
Protect the human part of the job
w5-mcq-9.q: 一家六人的 AI 初创企业让每位员工自行决定是否把客户记录粘贴到公共 AI 工具中。这最直接地违反了哪条 AI 时代的管理规则？
options: 更频繁地重新规划（re-plan more often）
在第一个客户之前写好数据规则（write data rules before the first customer）
保护工作中属于人的部分（protect the human part of the job）

w5-mcq-10.en: A social enterprise grows rapidly by shifting toward wealthier, more profitable customers and away from the communities it was founded to serve. This illustrates:
w5-mcq-10.q: 一家社会企业转向更富裕、利润更高的客户，偏离了它当初创立时要服务的社区，从而实现了快速增长。这说明了：
options: 使命需要利润（mission needs margin）
利润会侵蚀使命（margin can eat mission，即使命漂移 mission drift）

w5-mcq-11.en: Why does the lecture describe Grameen Bank as more than an act of kindness?
enOptions: It redesigned lending so customers labelled "unlendable" could become reliable borrowers
It charged the highest interest rates in Bangladesh
It required collateral from all borrowers
w5-mcq-11.q: 课程为什么把格莱珉银行（Grameen Bank）描述为不只是一种善举？
options: 它重新设计了放贷方式，使被贴上「不可放贷」标签的客户能够成为可靠的借款人
它收取孟加拉国最高的利率
它要求所有借款人提供抵押品

w5-mcq-12.en: When interviewing potential customers before building, which question is LEAST useful according to the lecture?
enOptions: How do you currently solve this problem?
How much time or money does it cost you?
What would make you switch solutions?
w5-mcq-12.q: 在动手构建之前访谈潜在客户时，根据课程内容，哪个问题最没有用？
options: 你目前是怎么解决这个问题的？
它让你花费多少时间或金钱？
什么会让你换用其他解决方案？

w5-mcq-13.en: A founder with no revenue yet needs funds for a product with high growth potential. Which financing approach does the lecture suggest is generally more suitable?
enOptions: Equity financing, because there is no fixed repayment obligation
A large bank loan, because interest rates are low
Debt, because founders keep all ownership
w5-mcq-13.q: 一位尚无收入的创始人需要资金来开发一款高增长潜力的产品。课程认为哪种融资方式通常更合适？
options: 股权融资（equity financing），因为没有固定的还款义务
大额银行贷款，因为利率低
债务（debt），因为创始人保留全部所有权
无限期使用个人信用卡

w5-mcq-14.en: A founder gives up 20% of the company in each of four funding rounds (simplified assumption). What share of the original holding remains?
w5-mcq-14.q: 一位创始人在四轮融资中每轮都出让公司 20% 的股份（简化假设）。她还剩原有持股的多少？

w5-mcq-15.en: A venture-backed company closes, reporting that it "ran out of capital". The lecture suggests the deeper cause is often:
w5-mcq-15.q: 一家风险投资支持的公司关闭了，报告称它「资金耗尽」。课程认为更深层的原因往往是：

w5-mcq-16.en: A firm is profitable and stable; its leaders are debating whether to slow down or push on. Which Churchill and Lewis stage is it in?
w5-mcq-16.q: 一家公司盈利且稳定；领导层正在争论是放慢脚步还是继续推进。它处于 Churchill 和 Lewis 模型的哪个阶段？

w5-mcq-17.en: A large, mature firm finds that every manager rationally protects existing products and new ideas stall. Which practice would the lecture recommend?
enOptions: Unallocated time, small bets, a route to implementation and survivable failure
Waiting for a crisis to force change
w5-mcq-17.q: 一家大型成熟企业发现，每位经理都理性地保护现有产品，新想法因此停滞。课程会推荐哪种做法？
options: 由委员会批准的一项大型创新赌注
不预先分配用途的时间、小赌注、通往实施的路径，以及可以承受的失败

w5-essay-0.en: Case: Two ANU students plan an app helping international students manage cross-border payments. They have spent three months building a polished version, funded by a family loan with no written terms. They have not spoken to any customers but say "everyone we know thinks it's a great idea". They now want to approach venture capitalists. Using Week 5 concepts, evaluate their approach and recommend next steps.
w5-essay-0.q: 案例：两名 ANU 学生计划开发一款应用，帮助国际学生管理跨境支付。他们已经花了三个月打磨出一个精致的版本，资金来自一笔没有书面条款的家庭借款。他们还没有和任何客户交谈过，但说「我们认识的每个人都觉得这是个好主意」。他们现在想去找风险投资人。请运用第 5 周的概念评价他们的做法，并建议下一步行动。

w5-essay-1.en: Case: A software start-up has grown from 6 to 60 staff in two years. The founder still approves every hire, reviews all customer-facing AI outputs personally and makes most product decisions; decisions now wait weeks. Staff increasingly use AI tools with no agreed rules, and a recent error in an AI-generated customer report became public. Investors are pushing for faster growth. Using Week 5 concepts, diagnose the issues and advise the founder.
w5-essay-1.q: 案例：一家软件初创企业在两年内从 6 名员工增长到 60 名。创始人仍然批准每一次招聘、亲自审核所有面向客户的 AI 输出，并做出大部分产品决策；现在决策要等上好几周。员工越来越多地在没有约定规则的情况下使用 AI 工具，最近一份 AI 生成的客户报告中的错误被公之于众。投资者正在施压，要求更快增长。请运用第 5 周的概念诊断问题，并为创始人提供建议。

w05-p01-0.en: Which of the following matches the lecture's definition of an entrepreneur?
enOptions: The process of initiating a venture and organising the necessary resources
A person who recognises an opportunity and commits their own resources and reputation to pursuing it
A new venture established to search for a repeatable and scalable business model
A manager who drives innovation inside an existing organisation
w05-p01-0.q: 以下哪一项符合课程对创业者（entrepreneur）的定义？
options: 发起一项事业并组织必要资源的过程
识别机会，并投入自己的资源和声誉去追求它的人
为寻找可重复、可规模化商业模式而建立的新企业
在现有组织内部推动创新的经理

w05-p01-1.en: Every new business is a start-up.
w05-p01-1.q: 每家新企业都是初创企业（start-up）。

w05-p01-2.en: Which of the following is most likely to be classified as a start-up in the lecture's sense?
enOptions: A two-person HR consultancy that bills by the day
An ANU biotech spin-out with a patent but no product or revenue yet
w05-p01-2.q: 按照课程中的含义，以下哪一项最有可能被归类为初创企业（start-up）？
options: Braddon 的一家单店咖啡馆
一家按天计费的两人人力资源咨询公司
一家拥有专利但尚无产品或收入的 ANU 生物技术衍生公司

w05-p01-3.en: The founder of a subscription software product says that if sign-ups doubled next month she would not need to hire anyone. Which property of the business is she describing?
w05-p01-3.q: 一款订阅制软件产品的创始人说，如果下个月注册量翻倍，她也不需要再招人。她描述的是企业的哪项属性？

w05-p01-4.en: Which statement best describes a 'repeatable' business model?
enOptions: The same way of creating and delivering value can happen again and again rather than being customised from scratch each time
Revenue can grow without costs growing in proportion
The venture is funded from savings and revenue
w05-p01-4.q: 哪种说法最能描述「可重复」（repeatable）的商业模式？
options: 同一种创造和交付价值的方式可以一次又一次地进行，而不是每次都从零开始定制
收入可以增长，而成本不按比例增长
企业由储蓄和收入提供资金

w05-p02-0.en: An independent consultant starts her own practice mainly so that she can control her own time. Using the growth-intent typology, she is a:
w05-p02-0.q: 一位独立顾问开办自己的事务所，主要是为了能掌控自己的时间。按照成长意图分类（growth-intent typology），她属于：
options: 生活方式型创业者（lifestyle entrepreneur）

w05-p02-1.en: In the survey of what business owners find most rewarding, which was the largest group, valuing doing something novel and creative?
w05-p02-1.q: 在关于企业主认为什么最有回报的调查中，人数最多、看重做新颖且有创意之事的是哪一类？

w05-p02-2.en: The lecture uses Canva and Atlassian as examples of growth entrepreneurs.
w05-p02-2.q: 课程用 Canva 和 Atlassian 作为成长型创业者（growth entrepreneurs）的例子。

w05-p02-3.en: A founder enjoys building companies: she sells one venture and immediately starts another. Which type is she?
w05-p02-3.q: 一位创始人喜欢创办公司：她卖掉一家企业后立刻又创办另一家。她属于哪种类型？

w05-p02-4.en: The 'Idealists' category in the rewards survey corresponds exactly to 'growth entrepreneurs' in the growth-intent typology.
w05-p02-4.q: 回报调查中的「理想主义者」（Idealists）类别，与成长意图分类中的「成长型创业者」（growth entrepreneurs）完全对应。

w05-p03-0.en: According to the lecture, industry experience often predicts entrepreneurial success better than youth.
w05-p03-0.q: 根据课程内容，行业经验往往比年轻更能预测创业成功。

w05-p03-1.en: A founder invests in stages, runs a small pilot before committing further, and uses investors' money rather than betting her own savings. How does the lecture describe this behaviour?
w05-p03-1.q: 一位创始人分阶段投入，在进一步投入前先做小规模试点，并使用投资者的钱而不是拿自己的积蓄下注。课程如何描述这种行为？
options: 承担经过计算的风险（taking calculated risk）

w05-p03-2.en: Two start-ups launch almost identical ideas in the same year; one succeeds and the other fails. According to the lecture, what most likely explains the difference?
enOptions: One of them had the more brilliant idea
w05-p03-2.q: 两家初创企业在同一年推出了几乎相同的想法；一家成功，另一家失败。根据课程内容，最可能解释这种差异的是什么？
options: 其中一家的想法更绝妙
创始人更年轻的那家赢了

w05-p03-3.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the three myths the lecture corrects?
enOptions: Entrepreneurial requirements are role demands that can be learned
w05-p03-3.q: 以下哪一项不属于课程纠正的三个迷思之一？
options: 成功需要一个绝妙的想法
创业要求是可以习得的角色要求

w05-p04-0.en: A two-person start-up rents servers by the hour and payment and logistics services by the month instead of buying them. Which change in the entrepreneurial context does this illustrate?
enOptions: Technology and infrastructure turning fixed costs into variable costs
w05-p04-0.q: 一家两人初创企业按小时租用服务器、按月租用支付和物流服务，而不是购买它们。这说明了创业环境的哪种变化？
options: 技术和基础设施把固定成本变成可变成本

w05-p04-1.en: Why can a small firm beat a large incumbent in a newly opened niche?
enOptions: It has speed, focus and flexibility, and no legacy product to protect
w05-p04-1.q: 为什么一家小公司能在一个新打开的细分市场中击败大型在位企业？
options: 它有速度、专注和灵活性，而且没有需要保护的既有产品

w05-p04-2.en: The small-firm advantage of speed and focus is permanent: once a firm has it, it keeps it as it grows.
w05-p04-2.q: 小公司在速度和专注上的优势是永久的：一旦拥有，公司成长后也会一直保有。

w05-p04-3.en: GEM reports that 18.5% of US adults are in early-stage entrepreneurial activity while established business ownership is 5.5%. How does the lecture say these figures should be read?
enOptions: Exactly 5.5 out of every 18.5 start-ups survive
As shares of different populations that support the heuristic that starting is easier than surviving, not a precise cohort survival rate
As proof that 18.5% of businesses fail each year
As evidence that established firms are more innovative
w05-p04-3.q: GEM 报告称，18.5% 的美国成年人处于早期创业活动中，而拥有成熟企业的比例为 5.5%。课程认为应如何解读这些数字？
options: 每 18.5 家初创企业中恰好有 5.5 家存活
它们是不同人群中的比例，支持「创业比存活容易」这一经验法则，而不是一个精确的同期群存活率
证明每年有 18.5% 的企业倒闭
证明成熟企业更具创新性

w05-p04-4.en: The lecture's overall judgement is that starting a business has become easier than before, but surviving has not become easier.
w05-p04-4.q: 课程的总体判断是：创业比以前更容易了，但存活并没有变得更容易。

w05-p05-0.en: In the lecture's words, if you cannot name the first customer, you have a theme rather than an opportunity.
w05-p05-0.q: 用课程的话说，如果你说不出第一个客户是谁，那你拥有的只是一个主题，而不是一个机会。

w05-p05-1.en: A student says: 'Canberra's new suburbs are growing fast, so there must be a business opportunity here.' According to the lecture, what is still missing?
enOptions: A specific unmet need, a value-creating product and a named first customer
w05-p05-1.q: 一名学生说：「堪培拉的新城区发展很快，所以这里一定有商机。」根据课程内容，还缺少什么？
options: 一个具体的未满足需求、一个能创造价值的产品和一个具名的第一个客户
一份完整的商业计划书

w05-p05-2.en: According to the lecture, which of the following is a good source of business ideas?
enOptions: Problems you repeatedly meet in your own work
Copying whatever the largest company does
Following any trend in the news
w05-p05-2.q: 根据课程内容，以下哪一项是商业想法的好来源？
options: 你在自己的工作中反复遇到的问题
随意头脑风暴产品名称
照搬最大的公司所做的一切
追随新闻中的任何趋势

w05-p05-3.en: A student proposes a storage and resale service for second-hand goods at ANU and names students leaving campus as the first customers. According to the lecture, what should happen next?
enOptions: Launch immediately, since the first customer is named
Test the idea against real constraints such as storage, licences, rent and operating costs
w05-p05-3.q: 一名学生提出在 ANU 开展二手物品存放和转售服务，并指明即将离开校园的学生为第一批客户。根据课程内容，接下来应该做什么？
options: 立即上线，因为第一个客户已经明确了
用真实的限制条件来检验这个想法，比如存放空间、许可证、租金和运营成本

w05-p06-0.en: Because a wrong version can now be killed in days for the price of a subscription, what does the lecture say a founder should do differently?
enOptions: Make one bigger unvalidated bet with the money saved
Run more small, cheap tests before committing
Skip customer interviews, since building is cheap
w05-p06-0.q: 既然现在一个错误的版本只需付一份订阅费、几天之内就能被淘汰，课程认为创始人应该做出什么不同的做法？
options: 用省下的钱下一个更大的、未经验证的赌注
在投入之前进行更多小而便宜的测试
既然构建很便宜，就跳过客户访谈

w05-p06-1.en: Two apps with nearly identical features launch in the same month. According to the lecture, what most likely decides which one survives?
enOptions: Which one has more lines of code
Distribution, trust and judgment about what is worth producing
Which one has the lower server bill
w05-p06-1.q: 两款功能几乎相同的应用在同一个月上线。根据课程内容，最可能决定哪一款存活的是什么？
options: 哪一款的代码行数更多
分销、信任，以及对什么值得生产的判断
哪一款的服务器账单更低

w05-p06-2.en: Lower barriers to entry cut both ways: they let you in, and they let everyone else in behind you.
w05-p06-2.q: 更低的进入门槛是一把双刃剑：它让你进来，也让其他所有人跟在你后面进来。

w05-p06-3.en: A start-up's main asset is detailed knowledge of its customers' habits gathered over three years of service. Which scarce advantage is this?
w05-p06-3.q: 一家初创企业的主要资产，是它在三年服务中积累的关于客户习惯的详细知识。这是哪种稀缺优势？
options: 专有数据和关系（proprietary data and relationships）

w05-p06-4.en: A client keeps buying from a small agency instead of using a free AI tool because, in her words, 'if something goes wrong, someone answers for it'. Which scarce advantage is she paying for?
w05-p06-4.q: 一位客户一直从一家小代理公司购买服务，而不使用免费的 AI 工具，因为用她的话说，「出了问题，有人负责」。她在为哪种稀缺优势付费？

w05-p07-0.en: An AI-drafted quote containing a wrong price went straight to a client; nobody had been assigned to check it. Which AI-era rule was broken?
enOptions: Protect the human part of the job
w05-p07-0.q: 一份由 AI 起草、价格有误的报价单被直接发给了客户；没有人被指派去检查它。违反了哪条 AI 时代的规则？
options: 更频繁地重新规划（re-plan more often）
决定由谁核查（decide who verifies）
尽早说明规范（state the norms early）
保护工作中属于人的部分（protect the human part of the job）

w05-p07-1.en: A founder still runs a fixed twelve-month roadmap even though her team can now ship a new version every week. Which rule does the lecture say she is ignoring?
enOptions: Write data rules before the first customer
w05-p07-1.q: 一位创始人仍然执行一份固定的十二个月路线图，尽管她的团队现在每周都能发布新版本。课程认为她忽视了哪条规则？
options: 更频繁地重新规划（re-plan more often）
在第一个客户之前写好数据规则（write data rules before the first customer）
决定由谁核查（decide who verifies）

w05-p07-2.en: A remote five-person team never discussed how they work together; each member has quietly adopted different standards for quality and tool use. Which rule is most relevant?
enOptions: Protect the human part of the job
w05-p07-2.q: 一个五人远程团队从未讨论过如何协作；每个成员都悄悄采用了不同的质量标准和工具使用标准。哪条规则最相关？
options: 保护工作中属于人的部分（protect the human part of the job）
尽早说明规范（state the norms early）
更频繁地重新规划（re-plan more often）
决定由谁核查（decide who verifies）

w05-p07-3.en: The lecture recommends delegating customer conversations and hiring decisions entirely to AI tools so the founder can focus on strategy.
w05-p07-3.q: 课程建议把客户沟通和招聘决策完全交给 AI 工具，以便创始人专注于战略。

w05-p07-4.en: A start-up is about to sign its first customer, but nobody has decided what information may be entered into AI tools, what must never be entered, or who can approve exceptions. Which rule is being neglected?
enOptions: Write data rules before the first customer
w05-p07-4.q: 一家初创企业即将签下第一个客户，但还没有人决定哪些信息可以输入 AI 工具、哪些绝不能输入，以及谁可以批准例外。哪条规则被忽视了？
options: 决定由谁核查（decide who verifies）
在第一个客户之前写好数据规则（write data rules before the first customer）
更频繁地重新规划（re-plan more often）
尽早说明规范（state the norms early）

w05-p08-0.en: Who Gives A Crap sells toilet paper and commits a fixed share of its profit to sanitation projects in developing countries. Why does the lecture classify this as social entrepreneurship rather than charity?
enOptions: Because it relies entirely on donors
Because it earns revenue through trade and measures part of its success by impact
Because it is a non-profit organisation
Because it does not have to compete on price
w05-p08-0.q: Who Gives A Crap 销售卫生纸，并承诺将固定比例的利润投入发展中国家的卫生设施项目。课程为什么把它归类为社会创业（social entrepreneurship）而不是慈善？
options: 因为它完全依赖捐赠者
因为它通过交易赚取收入，并部分以影响力来衡量成功
因为它不必在价格上竞争

w05-p08-1.en: A social venture loses money every year and eventually has to close its literacy programme. Which tension does this illustrate?
w05-p08-1.q: 一家社会企业年年亏损，最终不得不关闭其扫盲项目。这说明了哪种张力？
options: 使命需要利润（mission needs margin）
利润会侵蚀使命（margin can eat mission）

w05-p08-2.en: Why does the lecture say a social enterprise's impact must be measured, citing B Corp certification as an example?
enOptions: Because commitments, published results and external standards make mission drift visible
w05-p08-2.q: 课程为什么说社会企业的影响力必须被衡量，并以 B Corp 认证为例？
options: 因为承诺、公布的结果和外部标准能让使命漂移（mission drift）变得可见

w05-p08-3.en: The lecture presents Grameen Bank's microcredit mainly as an act of kindness rather than as a redesign of how lending risk is managed.
w05-p08-3.q: 课程把格莱珉银行（Grameen Bank）的小额信贷主要描述为一种善举，而不是对放贷风险管理方式的重新设计。

w05-p08-4.en: A strong social mission excuses a social enterprise from competing on price, packaging and distribution.
w05-p08-4.q: 强大的社会使命使社会企业可以免于在价格、包装和分销上竞争。

w05-p09-0.en: According to the lecture, at which of the five launch steps do new ventures most often lose their way?
enOptions: Validating the idea against real customers
w05-p09-0.q: 根据课程内容，新企业最常在五个创办步骤中的哪一步迷失方向？

w05-p09-1.en: A founder shows a mock-up to twenty friends, and all of them say they love it. She treats this as proof of demand. What does the lecture say?
enOptions: Twenty positive responses are sufficient evidence
Stated interest is weak evidence; a deposit, paid pre-order or signed letter of intent is much stronger
She needs at least fifty friends
She should seek venture capital first
w05-p09-1.q: 一位创始人把样品模型给二十个朋友看，他们都说很喜欢。她把这当作存在需求的证明。课程怎么说？
options: 二十个正面回应就是足够的证据
口头表示的兴趣是弱证据；定金、付费预购或签署的意向书要有力得多
她至少需要五十个朋友
她应该先寻求风险投资

w05-p09-2.en: Slack grew out of a failed game studio and Instagram out of a check-in app. Which concept do these examples illustrate?
enOptions: A pivot: a deliberate change of product, customer or model based on what was learned
w05-p09-2.q: Slack 脱胎于一家失败的游戏工作室，Instagram 脱胎于一款签到应用。这些例子说明了哪个概念？
options: 转型（pivot）：根据所学到的东西，有意识地改变产品、客户或模式

w05-p09-3.en: What does the lecture say is the main output of a minimum viable product (MVP)?
enOptions: A polished first version ready for mass market
Learning from real customers using the smallest workable version
w05-p09-3.q: 课程认为最小可行产品（MVP）的主要产出是什么？
options: 一个可以面向大众市场的精致首版
通过最小可用版本从真实客户那里获得的学习

w05-p09-4.en: The key difference between a prototype and an MVP is that an MVP must be used by real customers and generate learning.
w05-p09-4.q: 原型（prototype）和 MVP 的关键区别在于，MVP 必须被真实客户使用并产生学习。

w05-p10-0.en: A freelance photographer registers an ABN and trades under her own name; legally she and the business are the same entity. Which structure is this?
w05-p10-0.q: 一位自由摄影师注册了 ABN，并以自己的名字经营；在法律上她和企业是同一个主体。这是哪种结构？

w05-p10-1.en: Two friends run a tutoring business under a written agreement, sharing profits and decisions, and each is personally liable for the business's debts. Which structure is this?
w05-p10-1.q: 两个朋友根据一份书面协议经营一家辅导业务，共享利润和决策，每人都对企业债务承担个人责任。这是哪种结构？

w05-p10-2.en: A start-up plans to raise venture capital next year. Which legal structure will investors typically require, and why?
enOptions: Sole trader, because it is cheapest
Company, because investors need to buy shares in a separate legal entity
Any structure, as long as it has an ABN
w05-p10-2.q: 一家初创企业计划明年融入风险投资。投资者通常会要求哪种法律结构？为什么？
options: 个体经营者，因为它最便宜
合伙企业，因为它可以共享资源
公司，因为投资者需要购买一个独立法律实体的股份
任何结构都行，只要有 ABN

w05-p10-3.en: Choosing a company structure guarantees that directors and founders can never be personally liable under any circumstances.
w05-p10-3.q: 选择公司结构可以保证董事和创始人在任何情况下都绝不会承担个人责任。

w05-p11-0.en: A café owner borrows from a bank and will repay the loan with interest over five years while keeping full ownership of the business. Which type of financing is this?
w05-p11-0.q: 一位咖啡馆老板向银行借款，将在五年内连本带息偿还，同时保留对企业的全部所有权。这是哪种融资？

w05-p11-1.en: An investor puts money into a start-up in exchange for 15% of its shares and a seat on the board. Which type of financing is this?
w05-p11-1.q: 一位投资者向一家初创企业投入资金，换取其 15% 的股份和一个董事会席位。这是哪种融资？

w05-p11-2.en: Debt is cheaper if the venture succeeds and dangerous if it does not; equity is the reverse.
w05-p11-2.q: 如果企业成功，债务（debt）更便宜；如果企业失败，债务就很危险；股权（equity）则正好相反。

w05-p11-3.en: A venture has stable, predictable revenue and the founder wants to keep full control. Which financing option fits best according to the lecture?
enOptions: Debt, such as a bank loan
w05-p11-3.q: 一家企业收入稳定、可预测，创始人希望保留全部控制权。根据课程内容，哪种融资方式最合适？
options: 风险投资股权（venture capital equity）
债务，如银行贷款（debt, such as a bank loan）

w05-p11-4.en: If a venture becomes extremely valuable, which form of financing turns out to have been the more expensive one?
enOptions: Debt, because interest grows with company value
Equity, because the shares given away are now worth a great deal
w05-p11-4.q: 如果一家企业变得极其值钱，事后看哪种融资形式更昂贵？
options: 债务，因为利息随公司价值增长
股权，因为出让的股份现在价值巨大

w05-p12-0.en: Government grants and incentives such as the R&D Tax Incentive are strictly a form of debt financing.
w05-p12-0.q: 研发税收激励（R&D Tax Incentive）等政府补助和激励措施严格来说属于债务融资（debt financing）。

w05-p12-1.en: An experienced former founder invests in a start-up before any venture capital firm is involved, and spends time advising the team and opening her network. Which source of financing is this?
w05-p12-1.q: 一位经验丰富的前创始人在任何风险投资机构介入之前投资了一家初创企业，并花时间为团队提供建议、开放自己的人脉。这是哪种资金来源？

w05-p12-2.en: Under the lecture's simplified assumption, a founder sells 20% of the company in each of four funding rounds. Roughly what share of the original holding does she keep?
w05-p12-2.q: 按照课程的简化假设，一位创始人在四轮融资中每轮都出售公司 20% 的股份。她大约保留原有持股的多少？

w05-p12-3.en: According to the lecture, what should a founding team aim to achieve between two funding rounds?
enOptions: Remove one specific risk that investors can clearly see
w05-p12-3.q: 根据课程内容，创始团队在两轮融资之间应该力求做到什么？
options: 消除一个投资者能清楚看到的具体风险
组建一支庞大的销售团队

w05-p12-4.en: A hardware start-up raises money through reward-based crowdfunding before manufacturing. Besides capital, what does the lecture say this provides?
enOptions: Evidence that customers will make a real commitment, or a cheap 'no' from the market before mass production
A board seat for the founder
w05-p12-4.q: 一家硬件初创企业在生产之前通过回报型众筹（reward-based crowdfunding）筹集资金。课程认为，除了资金之外，这还能提供什么？
options: 客户会做出真实承诺的证据，或者在大规模生产前就从市场得到一个代价低廉的「不」

w05-p13-0.en: Among the 431 venture-backed companies that closed after 2023, which reason was reported most often?
w05-p13-0.q: 在 2023 年后关闭的 431 家风险投资支持的公司中，哪个原因被报告得最多？
options: 单位经济效益不可持续（19%）

w05-p13-1.en: A board member says: 'Just raise another round and the problem is solved.' Based on the lecture, what is the flaw in this reasoning?
enOptions: Funding rounds are impossible after the second year
Funding delays death but does not fix a product nobody needs, unless the team pivots on evidence
Debt would always be better than another round
w05-p13-1.q: 一位董事会成员说：「再融一轮，问题就解决了。」根据课程内容，这一推理的缺陷是什么？
options: 第二年之后不可能再进行融资
融资只能推迟死亡，无法修好一个没人需要的产品，除非团队根据证据进行转型
债务总是比再融一轮更好
单位经济效益从来都不重要

w05-p13-2.en: Because 70% of closed companies ran out of capital and 43% reported poor product-market fit, the two reasons together account for 113% of closures.
w05-p13-2.q: 由于 70% 的已关闭公司资金耗尽、43% 报告产品市场契合差，这两个原因合计占关闭原因的 113%。

w05-p13-3.en: Which causal chain does the lecture describe for venture failure?
enOptions: Running out of capital causes poor product-market fit
Poor product-market fit, bad economics or timing make customers and investors stop supplying money, so capital runs out and the business closes
Bad timing causes dilution, which causes closure
Hiring professional managers causes capital shortage
w05-p13-3.q: 课程描述的企业失败因果链是哪一条？
options: 资金耗尽导致产品市场契合差
产品市场契合差、经济效益不佳或时机不对，使客户和投资者不再提供资金，于是资金耗尽、企业关闭
时机不好导致股权稀释，进而导致关闭
聘用职业经理人导致资金短缺

w05-p14-0.en: A firm has just begun offering its service, and the only question anyone asks is whether it will survive at all. Which Churchill and Lewis stage is this?
w05-p14-0.q: 一家公司刚刚开始提供服务，大家唯一关心的问题是它到底能不能活下来。这是 Churchill 和 Lewis 模型的哪个阶段？

w05-p14-1.en: A firm has reached a key expansion point; its leaders are asking how to finance growth and whether to hand day-to-day control to professional managers. Which stage is this?
w05-p14-1.q: 一家公司已到达一个关键的扩张节点；领导层在考虑如何为增长融资，以及是否把日常控制权交给职业经理人。这是哪个阶段？

w05-p14-2.en: A founder insists on approving every decision herself; the company cannot grow because everything waits on her. What does the lecture identify as the bottleneck?
enOptions: Delegation: the founder must move from doing the work to building people who direct the work
Too much diversity in the team
w05-p14-2.q: 一位创始人坚持每个决定都由自己批准；公司因为所有事都要等她而无法成长。课程认为瓶颈是什么？
options: 授权：创始人必须从亲自做事转变为培养指导工作的人

w05-p14-3.en: Bringing in professional managers at the take-off stage signals that the founder has failed.
w05-p14-3.q: 在起飞期（take-off）引入职业经理人，标志着创始人失败了。

w05-p14-4.en: The lecture says that growth costs flexibility. What does it say buys some of that flexibility back?
enOptions: Intrapreneurship: unallocated time, small bets, a route to implementation and survivable failure
w05-p14-4.q: 课程说增长会以牺牲灵活性为代价。它认为什么能把部分灵活性买回来？
options: 内部创业（intrapreneurship）：不预先分配用途的时间、小赌注、通往实施的路径，以及可以承受的失败
